sharedSkillEdits.edits: `SKILL.md` states that a prompt or brief naming the skill is its invocation.
It adds a Reads section, which lists the repository files the skill reads and what it does when each is missing.

code-review.edits: It also drops the route to `setup-matt-pocock-skills` when the tracker configuration is missing, and its spec search reviews against the issue's implementation contract where the tracker configuration says which comment or body holds it. It pins both comparison commits and the merge-base, runs the bundled ownership-facts.mjs collector before the independent axes, and passes its facts and codebase-design's Ownership check to Standards. The collector runs through symbolic links and stays inert when imported. Both prompts apply that section's cleanup allowance against the PR body and retain contract-based judgment and the planning rules' Findings route. Spec discovery follows the validator’s selected source/revision and prepared/body-mode rules, including only the exact unchanged inventoried legacy exception; later comments cannot replace a migrated body contract. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback.

codebase-design.edits: It adds the shared Ownership check section: value owners, triggers and cost read, wrapping and extraction defaults, deferred seams, narrow touched-code cleanup, contract disagreement routing, and capability/policy and vendored UI examples. Its description and Reads section expose that reference. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback.

domain-modeling.edits: It also has glossary and ADR edits made on a branch of their own in a checkout the session owns, never in a shared checkout on the default branch, and delivered as the repository's contribution guide directs. It creates `docs/adr/` with its index where the repo indexes its documentation directories, and `ADR-FORMAT.md` adds each new ADR to that index, and keeps a superseded ADR, marking it superseded with a link to the ADR that supersedes it.

grill-with-docs.edits: It composes grilling and domain-modeling with to-spec then to-tickets, publishing one cross-repository specification and proposed direct tickets for independent exact-revision review. It reuses dated decisions, applies the planning rules’ decision rights, reports native-link failures, and handles amendment grills through specification revisions and delta tickets, with Reads fallbacks. It invokes codebase-design and applies its single Ownership check to proposed designs during the interview. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback. It names the role-selected other party and passes the proposed specification and split into grilling’s publishing final round, retaining strategic review and recorded-approval reuse.

grilling.edits: It also asks the frontier in rounds and keeps each round short, asking the frontier questions that unblock the most first when the frontier holds more than the user can weigh at once. It reuses recorded dated answers, selects each round’s decision maker through the planning rules, and retains grill-answer and plan-approval gates without an extra quiz. It may build a throwaway prototype with the `prototype` skill when words cannot settle a look or how a state model feels, and a grill that adds or changes a mechanism or policy ends with an independent review against long-term design, asked as its final round. A composite skill continues to publication after the interview; its Reads section supplies the contribution-guide fallback. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback. Both standalone and composite grills identify the maintainer or delegated agent as their other party. Its publishing final round combines the existing strategic review with the specification repository, ticket split, repositories, blockers, testing seams and publication go-ahead, reuses applicable recorded approval and reopens when required questions return.

implement.edits: `SKILL.md` drops `disable-model-invocation` and `agents/openai.yaml` enables `policy.allow_implicit_invocation`. It reads branch and validation requirements from the contribution guide. It replaces self-review and direct delivery with validated draft pull request creation using `pr`, then stops for a separate `review` agent. Given review findings, it pushes fixes to the same draft pull request and stops again. A factory without a configured review run retains delivery through `babysit` under its installed rules, including applicable internal reviews, merge conditions and worker handoffs. Both routes require the contribution guide's Worker handoff record; separate review applies the factory environment-step rule to the passing-checks condition. It keeps that record as the pull request body's Delivery subsection, updated on each push, and reports one lead line naming the pull request and its check state. At `self-reported`, its own check command result and the PR metadata entry point's status make the handoff, which never waits on or posts `Review rerun`. Installed rules select delivery; factory configuration reads are removed. Without a contribution guide, it uses a dedicated branch and available checks before opening the draft. It applies codebase-design’s single Ownership check to its change, including that section’s contract-disagreement route, with a missing-skill fallback in Reads. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback. Delegation and session naming move from agent guidance into this skill's `DELEGATION.md` reference.

improve-codebase-architecture.edits: It also makes the grilling loop's domain-model edits on the branch and checkout `domain-modeling` directs. Named ownership exploration uses codebase-design's Ownership check for misplaced values, configuration kinds and surprising layout, passing that reference to its exploring sub-agent. An orchestrated launch writes Markdown candidates to its designated report and stops before the HTML report and grilling loop.

pr.edits: Evidence requires screenshots on an orphan `pr-assets/<topic>` branch and image links by full commit SHA, and refers to the installed GitHub repository configuration rules for permanent asset-branch retention during cleanup, preserving the branch when those rules are missing. Its template ends with a Related issue section after Merge Danger, holding a closing or partial-work reference or a Direct change reason, and keeps the four sections in order with any other material in a subsection of the section it belongs to. Evidence lists every check run on the final commit with its outcome and explains any required check not run, and Merge Danger names the change's relevant limits and a breaking change's impact and migration. Summary condenses the visual examples while retaining every visual type and its selection, context, placement and copyable-target guidance. This file keeps upstream's credits below unchanged. The `show-me` material those credits name is covered by HumanLayer's MIT License, whose notice follows Matt Pocock's at the end of this file; adoption also installs it beside the skills.

research.edits: Its description covers assigned artifacts and delegated triage research. The current run performs the investigation directly, including when delegated, instead of starting another background researcher. It publishes an assigned artifact at its destination with source citations; an issue artifact needs no repository findings file or index edit. Without an assigned artifact, it defaults to a single Markdown findings file where the repository's documentation rules or convention put such notes, such as beside the usage or development topic they serve, and adds it to that directory's index, creating it when those rules require one. It retains the missing-rules placement fallback. An issue or pull request artifact is posted as the installed comment rules' section it names says.

to-spec.edits: It also drops the route to `setup-matt-pocock-skills` when the tracker configuration is missing, and publishes the spec awaiting an independent readiness review, after any revision notice and with the labels the repository's rules require, instead of applying `ready-for-agent` itself; a spec broken into tickets gets its readiness after they are published. Each step that publishes an issue body or posts a comment on a hosted tracker names the installed comment rules' section to read first. It replaces test-seam re-confirmation with dated decision reuse and evidence for independent review, routes only unresolved owner choices, and publishes one direct issue-body specification in the repository containing most work. It copies decision dates and quoted words, returns the published or amended specification to its caller for ticket sequencing, and handles amendments with fresh revision review and readiness. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback.

to-tickets.edits: It also drops both routes to `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. Expand–contract batches that cannot each stay green become one ticket instead of sharing an integration branch, since every ticket merges on its own with its checks passing. On a real tracker, parent and blocker links are native only, and a link that cannot be created is reported instead of written into the body. Tickets are published awaiting an independent readiness review instead of carrying `ready-for-agent`, and the local ticket template's status is `state:triage`. Live evidence follows the contribution guide's rule: it stays on the source ticket unless the work splits into a source ticket and a live-acceptance ticket that no merge closes, and nobody edits a ready ticket to record progress. A ticket that switches one side of a cross-repository break is blocked by its own tickets for each release, adopter update and host step it needs, in the repositories that own them, and blocks the recovery ticket of any repository it deliberately pauses; the split's review evidence checks those steps against each intervening deployed state, and host values stay in owner setup. Each step that publishes an issue body or posts a comment on a hosted tracker names the installed comment rules' section to read first. It replaces the owner breakdown quiz with evidence for independent split review and the planning rules’ final split authority. Grill publication uses one specification parent across responsible repositories, copies dated decisions and quoted words, reports exact native-link failures, applies the full inference boundary and handles authorized delta amendments with renewed exact-revision readiness. Blocking edges for overlapping writes are drawn only when two tickets rewrite the same authored passage or shared inventory, with the reason in **Blocked by**, and a deletion ticket goes ahead of tickets editing its surface. Deepening tickets are a second exception to vertical slicing, stating a structural outcome and listed behaviour changes, one criterion naming what must no longer exist, and interface tests that keep passing; the Reads section adds `codebase-design` for that vocabulary. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback. UI, visual and icon ticket contracts include the design acceptance criteria through a link to triage’s Agent Brief method, keeping their definition in one home, and the Reads section declares that reference and its missing-file behavior.

triage.edits: `OUT-OF-SCOPE.md` and `agents/openai.yaml` are unchanged from it. The skill keeps upstream's invocation, discovery buckets, outcomes, and templates, and names its roles by Repo Canon's `state:` label family: five roles naming whom an issue waits on, `state:carried` for a request another record or ticket carries, and `wontfix` as the closing outcome. Upstream's `needs-info` becomes `state:reporter`, kept for a fact only an outside reporter holds, beside `state:grill` and `state:owner` for the owner's intent and answers; `ready-for-human` becomes `state:owner`, which is not readiness; and triage sets a `priority:` label by the installed rules' rubric without replacing a person's. It replaces the single triage procedure with routing by uncertainty: research and independent acceptance for code-bound requests, and for intent-bound ones fact-finding, bounded triager inference, and a grill with the decision maker selected by the planning rules that publishes direct specification/ticket contracts for independent review. It routes every question through the orchestrating agent: owner intent goes to its grill session, waiting in `state:grill` when the owner cannot join, while operational owner decisions and chores use the decision inbox. It points to the triage label configuration for tracker strings and the installed GitHub rules for categories and meanings instead of repeating their inventory, retaining the brief's categories and its routing and outcome fallbacks when rules are absent; it replaces the disclaimer with the installed comment rules' section that each posting step names, adds who does what, notes that a quick state override is the maintainer's own review applied through the readiness command, and has acceptance choose between `state:ready`, `state:ready` with the factory's skip label, and `state:owner`. The Reads section also covers `ready.mjs` and the installed comment rules. `AGENT-BRIEF.md` keeps upstream's principles, template, and examples, and adds the decisions, progress and live-evidence principles and the triage notes. Its reference condenses durability and behavioral guidance, repeated template placeholders, and bug, enhancement, PR and negative examples while retaining the original seven fields, every example contract, available-input and decision provenance, independent acceptance, owner-review designation and revision/readiness semantics. `ready.mjs` is Repo Canon's original readiness acceptance command. The acceptance step calls it to apply the reviewed revision and confirm the validator recorded it. The research handoff identifies the issue comments as the assigned research artifacts and destinations, composing with the research skill's direct investigation and assigned publication method. The code-bound brief followed by triage notes and intent-bound fact-finding notes remain distinct deliverables. Its accept mode, `triage accept <issue>`, reviews one contract's current revision, refuses when the reviewing session published it, posts one verdict comment and applies readiness through the readiness command when it holds. Another mode runs the skill unattended as the factory's triage run: it researches, writes and reviews the brief itself, cites only repository records for inferred intent, writes nothing on the tracker, and ends with a run result that asks the factory to post the brief, question or cited carrier and apply its labels. On a direct specification or ticket it writes no brief: when the body holds and the run did not write the issue, it asks the host to accept the exact reviewed revision with readiness labels; otherwise it ends in a stop with its review. The skill points to target planning rules for the triage policy instead of restating it. Its method consolidates mode and role summaries, folds resumption into context gathering, and states the reporter template and Reads fallbacks compactly while preserving the research, independent acceptance, readiness and factory-result procedures. Its Publication mode pointer reaches the installed GitHub rules’ Agent Brief policy and factory workflow rules’ Contract publication mode policy, replacing triage’s duplicate legacy-mode restatements without changing body contracts, cutoff, attestation or exact-revision acceptance. The template, examples and independent review add Seams after Out of scope, citing codebase-design’s single Ownership check definition. The writer records its result and independent review assesses honesty, Value owner, consumers, reversibility and cost, while the validator checks structure. The readiness command also checks body-observation freshness for v3 Seams exemption results. Its intent-bound grill publishes one specification and proposed direct tickets through to-spec/to-tickets, instead of draft Agent Briefs for the orchestrator to file. Independent acceptance checks the split and seam/factual evidence without an owner quiz, preserves original intake publication rules and applies direct-contract shapes without redundant briefs or category labels. It handles amendment revisions and exact native-link failures. Model suggestions, acceptance and the factory triage result cite the installed Model selection rule and record its guidance-based reason, bounded by supplied host capabilities. The readiness command provisions an explicitly requested missing factory skip label before applying readiness, sharing canonical metadata with label setup and retaining that dependency for installed execution. The brief template and examples open with the installed comment rules' lead line and carry no disclosure footer, the triage notes collapse behind a factual summary while owner questions and inferred intent stay visible, and a short-fields principle limits Summary, Current behavior, Desired behavior, list items and criteria. Planning policy is read from the target repository’s installed planning rules, with its contribution guide only as the non-adopter fallback. Delegation and session-naming discovery now points to the shared `.agents/skills/implement/DELEGATION.md` reference moved from agent guidance. Its Agent Brief method adds design acceptance outcomes for UI, visual and icon work, making the token plan, named-tell self-review, screenshot critique and reference-judged vector master observable on the pull request without fixing a canonical tell list or installing a design skill. `SKILL.md` keeps shared context gathering and routes the real orchestration, accept and unattended factory branches to `ORCHESTRATING.md`, `ACCEPT.md` and `FACTORY.md`; `REVIEW.md` holds their shared independent contract assessment. `AGENT-BRIEF.md` compresses principles and notes while retaining every example contract and design acceptance outcome.

wayfinder.edits: It also drops the route to `setup-matt-pocock-skills` when the tracker configuration is missing, counts only native child and blocking links on a tracker that has them, reporting a link that cannot be created, and fills every map section but Decisions so far, including Out of scope, with words rather than only its template comment. Each step that publishes an issue body or posts a comment on a hosted tracker names the installed comment rules' section to read first.

writing-for-agents.edits: Its pruning reference keeps requirements in the rules or contribution guide that hold them, with skills stating the method, and puts repository-specific agent constraints in the file a repository names for them where it installs `AGENTS.md` as shared content. Its skill-mechanics reference says that a prompt or brief naming a user-invoked skill is its invocation, whether a human, another skill's step or a delegation brief writes it: another skill reaching a skill no longer justifies model-invocation or a split, shared reference can live in a skill the others name, and a router's naming invokes the skill it picks.

docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.edits: Creating an issue writes the body in the matching issue form's sections and passes it as a body file. Reading an issue names the latest Agent Brief comment as its implementation contract. Readiness labels are applied only through the triage skill's readiness command. The Wayfinding map entry names the Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified and Out of scope sections the Wayfinder rules enforce, in place of the upstream Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. Wayfinding child and blocking links are native only: the task list, `Part of` and `Blocked by` body fallbacks are removed, an uncreatable link is reported, and the frontier query reads native sub-issues and dependencies.

docs/agents/triage-labels.md.edits: The two-column table maps upstream roles to Repo Canon's tracker strings, including grill and carried states with no upstream role. It points to the installed GitHub rules for canonical meanings, colors and descriptions and, where installed, the factory workflow rules for factory-profile additions. Repeated meanings, state and readiness rules and the closing invitation to edit the installed file are removed.
